failures.triage_note: The listing-map block's initial server render (blocks/listing-map/render.php) never reads the $_GET keyword/type filters the grid uses -- it only filters by the block's fixed listingType attribute and bounds. On the same Directory page with the same search applied, the map shows pins for listings that do not match the active search while the grid/result-count correctly report 0 or a different count. This is the map-vs-grid analogue of cross-cutting check 8 (a number/state must agree with what it represents).
failures.expected: Map markers reflect the same keyword+type filtered result set as the listing grid on the same page.
failures.actual: type=business&keyword=cafe: grid + REST /search both correctly return 0 results ('No listings found' empty state, computed-visible), but the embedded Leaflet map still shows 2 pins for non-matching Business listings. Separately, type=restaurant (no keyword): grid shows 26 real cards but the map shows only 3 marker/cluster icons -- the two surfaces are simply running independent, unsynced queries.
failures.evidence: REST curl: `curl "http://wb-listora.local/wp-json/listora/v1/search?type=business&keyword=cafe"` -> {"listings":[],"total":0,...} (matches grid). Screenshot at wp-content/plugins/wb-listora/fail-search-empty-state-with-results.png shows '0 results' / 'No listings found' text alongside 2 live map pins over Massachusetts/NY. Source check: `grep -n "\$_GET" blocks/listing-map/render.php` returns no hits for keyword/type -- only `bounds` is read (line ~70).

failures.triage_note: The plugin's own `wb_listora_dashboard_page_id` option correctly points at page ID 7 ('My Listings', slug /my-listings/), which renders the full 2-column sidebar+main dashboard (grid, 260px sidebar, all tabs, correct stats) exactly per contract, and the site's primary nav links there too. However a SEPARATE page exists at the URL the runbook's Global Preconditions and this CORE row both name as canonical (`/dashboard/`, post ID 3642, title 'Dashboard') whose content is the literal unrendered shortcode text `[directorist_user_dashboard]` -- a leftover from Directorist competitor-migration testing on this dev site, not a Listora template. Likely environment/fixture pollution rather than a shipped plugin defect, but flagged because (a) it means a customer following the documented dashboard URL on THIS site sees a broken page, and (b) it reveals the runbook's assumed dashboard slug no longer matches this site's actual configuration -- worth a source-of-truth check on a genuinely fresh install.
failures.expected: /dashboard/ renders the Listora 2-column member dashboard (My Listings, Reviews, Favorites, Claims, Credits, Profile tabs).
failures.actual: /dashboard/ (logged in as contributor1) renders only the plain-text string '[directorist_user_dashboard]' inside .entry-content -- no dashboard UI, no tabs, no listings. The working dashboard is at /my-listings/ instead.
failures.evidence: wp post get 3642 --field=post_content => '[directorist_user_dashboard]'. wp option get wb_listora_dashboard_page_id => 7 (My Listings). getComputedStyle check at /my-listings/ confirmed .listora-page--dashboard renders display:grid, gridTemplateColumns:'260px 986px' -- correct 2-column layout, just at a different URL than /dashboard/.

failures.triage_note: The listing-detail Save button's favorite-count badge (`<span class="listora-detail__favorite-count">`) is server-rendered once with no `data-wp-text`/`data-wp-bind` reactive binding, so IAPI's toggleFavorite action correctly flips is-favorited/aria-pressed/aria-label but never touches the count span. A full page reload shows the correct count, proving this is a client-side reactivity gap, not a persistence bug. This is exactly the counter/state-disagreement class cross-cutting check 8 exists to catch.
failures.expected: Favorites count on the Save button updates client-side immediately after toggling (per runbook: 'Favorites count on the heart button updates client-side').
failures.actual: Before toggle: DB has 1 favorite for the listing, button shows 'Save 1'. After clicking Save (POST /favorites succeeds, is-favorited=true, aria-pressed=true): DB now has 2 favorites (verified via `SELECT * FROM wp_listora_favorites WHERE listing_id=31` -- 2 rows) but the visible badge still reads 'Save 1'. Reloading the page shows 'Save 2' (correct, server-rendered).
failures.evidence: Button outerHTML before/after toggle: `1` unchanged despite `aria-pressed` flipping false->true and a 201-equivalent successful POST to /wp-json/listora/v1/favorites. Post-reload the same span reads 2, and `wp db query "SELECT * FROM wp_listora_favorites WHERE listing_id=31"` returns 2 rows (user_id 5 pre-existing + user_id 6 added by the test click).
